paragraphs.en: By God, my lady, I was not born one-eyed. My father was a king who taught me to read the Magnificent Quran proficiently. I then studied jurisprudence and calligraphy, surpassing all contemporaries.
paragraphs.zh: 天哪，夫人，我可不是生来就一只眼睛看不见。我的父亲是一位国王，他教会了我熟练地阅读《宏伟的古兰经》。随后我又研习了法学和书法，远远超过了同时代的所有人。

paragraphs.en: My fame spread far and wide.
paragraphs.zh: 我的名声传遍了四方。

paragraphs.en: One day, the king of India sent gifts and messengers to my father, requesting that he send me. My father prepared six horses for the journey, and we set out with couriers. After a month's ride, we encountered fifty armored horsemen who appeared like lions in steel armor.
paragraphs.zh: 一天，印度国王派人送来礼物和使者，要求将我送去宫廷。父亲为此准备了六匹骏马，我们带着信使上路了。一个月后，我们在途中遇到了五十名全副武装的骑士，他们身穿铁甲，如同钢铸的雄狮一般威武。

paragraphs.en: But morning interrupted Shahrazad, and she paused. Her sister then said, "Sister, what an amazing story!" Shahrazad replied, "Wait until tomorrow night if I stay alive!"
paragraphs.zh: 但是黎明打断了沙赫札德，她停了下来。她的妹妹随后说道：“姐姐，这真是个惊人的故事！”沙赫札德回答道：“如果我活到明天晚上，你再听吧！”

paragraphs.en: The following night, Dinarzad requested a tale from Shahrazad. She began: When we approached the highwaymen, they revealed themselves as robbers. Seeing our small company with goods, they mistook us for carrying money and attacked.
paragraphs.zh: 当晚，迪纳兹德向舍赫拉扎德请求一个故事。舍赫拉扎德开始讲述：当我们接近那些强盗时，他们露出了真面目。看到我们这个小队带着货物，误以为我们身上携带着钱财，于是便发动了袭击。

paragraphs.en: My men were killed, but I escaped, wandering without direction.
paragraphs.zh: 我的手下被杀，但我侥幸逃脱，四处流浪，毫无方向。

paragraphs.en: I went from being mighty to lowly, rich to poor.
paragraphs.zh: 我从权势跌落为卑微，由富有变得一贫如洗。

paragraphs.en: The following night, Shahrazad began her tale:
paragraphs.zh: 当晚，舍赫拉查德开始了她的讲述：

paragraphs.en: O happy king, said Shahrazad, the second dervish told a girl that after being robbed, he continued his journey. As night fell, he found shelter in a cave on a mountain until dawn. He traveled for a month, surviving on plants and fruits, before reaching a bustling city teeming with life.
paragraphs.zh: 贤明的国王，第二位圣士对一个女孩说，在被抢劫后，他继续上路。夜幕降临，他在山洞中暂避风霜，直到天亮。他走了整整一个月，靠采集野果和植物为生，终于来到了一个生机勃勃、人声鼎沸的城市。

paragraphs.en: The arrival of spring filled the city with beauty: flowing streams, blooming flowers, and singing birds.
paragraphs.zh: 春天的到来让整座城市充满了生机与美丽：潺潺的溪流，绽放的花朵，以及鸣叫的鸟儿。

paragraphs.en: The dervish felt both joy and sorrow. Joy at arriving in the city, but sadness over his wretched condition—pale from exhaustion, chapped hands and feet, and overwhelmed by worry. He entered the city unsure of where to go until he passed a tailor's shop.
paragraphs.zh: 苦乐交织，修士的心情复杂难言。他抵达城市时感到欣喜，但又为自己的糟糕状况而忧伤——脸色因疲劳而苍白，手脚干裂，满心忧虑无处安放。他在城中茫然不知所措，直到路过一家裁缝店。

paragraphs.en: The tailor welcomed him, asked about his story, and felt sorry for him. The tailor warned that the king was their greatest enemy due to a blood feud.
paragraphs.zh: 裁缝热情地迎接了他，询问了他的遭遇，并对他表示同情。裁缝警告说，由于家族间的宿怨，国王是他们最大的敌人。

paragraphs.en: They shared food together, and when it grew dark, the tailor offered the dervish a place in his shop to sleep, providing a blanket and other necessities.
paragraphs.zh: 他们一起分享食物，天黑后裁缝主动让德威什在店铺里过夜，并为他准备了毯子和其他必需品。

paragraphs.en: He asked me after three days: "Don't you have any skill to earn a living?" I replied, "I am a jurist, poet, grammarian, and calligrapher." He said, "Such skills are not much in demand here."
paragraphs.zh: 他三天后问我：“你难道没有一技之长吗？”我回答说：“我是法学家、诗人、语法学家和书法家。”他说道：“这些技能在这里并不吃香。”

paragraphs.en: I responded, "By God, these are my only skills."
paragraphs.zh: 我说：“真主作证，这些就是我所有的本事了。”

paragraphs.en: He instructed me to prepare for a new life: "Gird yourself, take an axe and rope, and go hew wood in the wilderness. Keep your secret until relief comes from God." He provided me with tools and assigned me to work with woodcutters.
paragraphs.zh: 他吩咐我准备迎接新生活：“束紧腰带，拿上斧头和绳索，到荒野中砍柴。直到上帝赐予解脱之前，一定要保守你的秘密。”他给了我工具，并让我与樵夫们一起工作。

paragraphs.en: For a year, I cut wood daily, carrying my bundle back home. I sold it for half a dinar and brought the money to the tailor.
paragraphs.zh: 一年里，我每天砍柴，扛着一捆木头回家。卖了半迪纳后，我把钱拿去给裁缝做衣服。

paragraphs.en: One day, while deep in the woods, I found a tree stump. Digging around it, I discovered a ring attached to a wooden plank. Lifting the plank revealed a staircase leading down to an underground palace.
paragraphs.zh: 一天，我深入森林中行走时，发现了一块树桩。在周围挖掘，竟然在木板上找到了一枚戒指。抬起木板后，露出了通向地底宫殿的阶梯。

paragraphs.en: The palace was magnificent, with beautiful designs and a radiant beauty inside.
paragraphs.zh: 宫殿宏伟壮观，内部装饰精美，光彩夺目。

paragraphs.en: I saw a girl who was five feet tall, with a graceful figure, firm breasts, soft cheeks, and fair skin. Her hair shone like a pearl or the sun, her speech banished sorrow, and even wise men were captivated by her. The poet described her as:
paragraphs.zh: 我见到一个身高五尺、身材修长的女孩，胸部挺拔，脸颊柔嫩，皮肤白皙。她的头发如同珍珠般闪耀，又似阳光般璀璨，言语间仿佛能驱散忧愁，连智者也被她深深吸引。诗人如此描述她：

paragraphs.en: Four things that never meet do here unite To shed my blood and to ravage my heart, A radiant brow and tresses that beguile And rosy cheeks and a glittering smile.
paragraphs.zh: 四者在此相聚，既不相交：它们令我心神俱疲，魂牵梦萦；一双明媚的双眸和秀发令人着迷，两抹红润的颊晕与闪烁的微笑。

paragraphs.en: But morning came, and Shahrazad fell silent. Dinarzad said, "Sister, what a strange and entertaining story!" She replied, "This is nothing compared to the tale I will tell you tomorrow night if the king spares me."
paragraphs.zh: 但黎明来临，沙赫札德默不作声。丁纳扎德说道：“姐姐，这故事真是离奇有趣！”她回答说：“比起我明天晚上如果国王饶恕我还要讲的故事来，这根本不算什么。”

paragraphs.en: The next night, Dinarzad asked her sister Shahrazad, "Tell us one of your tales." Shahrazad agreed.
paragraphs.zh: 第二天晚上，迪纳兹达对她的姐姐莎赫拉扎德说：“给我们讲一个你的故事吧。”莎赫拉扎德答应了。

paragraphs.en: Shahrazad began: The second dervish spoke to a girl. When she looked at him, she questioned, "Are you human or demon?" He replied, "I am human."
paragraphs.zh: 沙海拉扎德说道：第二个苦行僧与一个女孩交谈。女孩打量着他，问道：“你是人还是妖魔？”他回答说：“我是人。”

paragraphs.en: He continued, "My misfortune brought me here to ease my sorrow, perhaps yours can do the same." He shared his story of hardship, and she felt sorry for him.
paragraphs.zh: 他接着说：“我的不幸把我带到了这里，希望能减轻我的悲伤，也许你的也能起到同样的作用。”于是他讲述了自己坎坷的经历，她不禁为他感到同情。

paragraphs.en: She then said, "I too have a tale. I am Aftimarus' daughter from Ebony Island. On my wedding night, a demon took me away.
paragraphs.zh: 她接着说：“我也有一个故事。我是埃菲马鲁斯的女儿，来自黑玉岛。在出嫁之夜，一个恶魔将我带走了。”

paragraphs.en: For twenty-five years, he has cared for me, visiting every ten days. If you wish, spend five days with me before the demon returns."
paragraphs.zh: 他照顾我已经二十五年了，每隔十天来看我一次。如果你愿意的话，在妖魔回来之前和我一起待五天吧。

paragraphs.en: The dervish agreed, saying, "If only dreams were true."
paragraphs.zh: 德维什应允道：“但愿梦境成真。”

paragraphs.en: She bathed me and dressed me in a new gown. Afterward, she seated me on a couch and offered juice to drink while conversing with me. She then brought food for me to eat until I was full.
paragraphs.zh: 她给我洗了澡，换上了一套新衣服。之后，她在沙发上让我坐下，边聊天边递给我果汁喝。接着，她端来了食物，直到我吃饱为止。

paragraphs.en: When I rested, she massaged my back, and I fell asleep, forgetting all worries.
paragraphs.zh: 当我休息时，她为我按摩后背，不知不觉中我就睡着了，忘却了一切烦恼。

paragraphs.en: Upon waking later, she asked if I was ready to drink. We drank together until nightfall, spending a delightful evening that surpassed any in my life. The next day, we continued our revelry until midday, where I became so intoxicated that I nearly lost consciousness and staggered around.
paragraphs.zh: 醒来后，她问我是否准备好了喝酒。我们一同畅饮，直到夜幕降临，度过了一个令我难忘的愉快夜晚，远超以往任何时光。第二天，我们的狂欢持续到中午，我喝得酩酊大醉，几乎晕了过去，东倒西歪地走动着。

paragraphs.en: I said, "My beautiful one, let me carry you up from this prison." She laughed and replied, "O my lord, sit still and be content; only one out of ten days is for the demon."
paragraphs.zh: 我说：“我的美丽之人，让我带你从这囚笼中解脱出来。”她笑了笑回答道：“哦，我的主人，请您安坐于此，心满意足吧；只有十分之一的日子是属于妖魔的。”

paragraphs.en: In my drunken state, I kicked the step with my foot.
paragraphs.zh: 在醉酒状态下，我一脚踢开了台阶。

paragraphs.en: The next night, Dinarzad urged Shahrazad: "Sister, if you are not sleepy, tell us one of your charming tales." She agreed.
paragraphs.zh: 第二天晚上，迪纳兹德催促莎赫拉泽达：“姐姐，如果你不困的话，给我们讲一个动听的故事吧。”莎赫拉泽达答应了。

paragraphs.en: Shahrazad recounted the second dervish's tale. Upon kicking a step, he encountered thunder and lightning, causing the earth to shake and darkness to fall. Terrified, he fled up the stairs but left his sandals and axe behind.
paragraphs.zh: 沙弗拉扎德讲述了第二位苦行僧的故事。他刚跨出一步，便遭遇雷电交加，大地震颤，一片漆黑。吓得他脱口而出，急忙跑上楼梯，却把鞋和斧头忘在了原地。

paragraphs.en: Reaching the top, he saw the palace floor split asunder with a demon emerging. The demon accused him of troubling it, claiming the girl had drunk wine and stumbled.
paragraphs.zh: 到达顶端，他看到宫殿的地板裂开，一个恶魔从中出现。恶魔指责他搅扰了这里，声称那女孩喝醉了酒，跌倒了。

paragraphs.en: The dervish heard her cries from outside, trembling in fear. He replaced the trapdoor and covered it with earth, feeling sorrow for the girl's fate. Reflecting on his own life, he wept over how fortune turned against him, leading him to become a woodcutter before briefly prospering again only to face misfortune once more.
paragraphs.zh: 修道士听到她在外的呼救声，心中充满了恐惧。他重新安置了地窖盖，并用泥土覆盖好，为那女孩的命运感到悲伤。回想起自己的人生经历，他不禁为命运的反复无常而落泪，从一个伐木工一跃成为富人，却又再次遭遇不幸。

paragraphs.en: The second dervish turned on me with anger, eager to punish my rashness. I found my friend the tailor anxiously waiting for me. He was relieved to see me and asked where I had stayed last night.
paragraphs.zh: 第二位圣士怒气冲冲地转向我，急于惩罚我的鲁莽。我发现裁缝朋友焦急地等着我。见到我平安归来，他松了口气，问我昨晚住在哪里。

paragraphs.en: I thanked him for his concern and retired to reflect on what had happened.
paragraphs.zh: 我感谢他的关心，随后退了下来，思索刚才发生的事情。

paragraphs.en: My friend then told me that an old Persian gentleman had brought my iron axe and sandals to the woodcutters, claiming he found them near the mosque. The woodcutters recognized the axe as mine and directed the man to my shop entrance. As we spoke, the floor split open, revealing the very demon in disguise.
paragraphs.zh: 我的朋友告诉我，一位老波斯绅士将我的铁斧和木屐带到了樵夫们那里，声称是在清真寺附近找到的。樵夫们认出了那把斧子是我的，并指引那人来到我的店铺入口。就在这时，地面突然裂开，露出了那个伪装成人的恶魔。

paragraphs.en: Morning came, interrupting Shahrazad's tale. Dinarzad then said, "Sister, what a strange and entertaining story!" Shahrazad replied that it was nothing compared to what she would tell the next night if the king spared her life.
paragraphs.zh: 晨光熹微，打断了沙赫拉兹德的故事。迪纳扎德说道：“姐姐，这真是一个奇怪而有趣的故事！”沙赫拉兹德回应说，与她若能保住性命，隔夜再讲的故事相比，这不过是小巫见大巫罢了。

paragraphs.en: The following night, Dinarzad asked Shahrazad for another story. She agreed and began: The second dervish spoke to the girl, telling her...
paragraphs.zh: 当晚，迪纳兹德又向莎赫札德请求一个故事。她应允了，开始讲述：第二个苦行僧对女孩说……

paragraphs.en: The demon snatched me from my hiding place, soared into the sky, and flew away with me. After landing, he split the ground with his foot and plunged underground, emerging in the palace where I had spent the night.
paragraphs.zh: 那个恶魔一把将我从藏身之处抓起，腾空而起，带着我飞走了。落地后，他一脚踏裂地面，钻入地下，最终出现在我昨晚住宿的宫殿中。

paragraphs.en: Inside, I saw a naked girl tied up and bleeding. My eyes filled with tears as I watched her. The demon untied her and covered her, demanding, "Isn't this man your lover?"
paragraphs.zh: 里面，我看见一个赤身裸体的女孩被绑着，鲜血直流。我的眼中不禁涌出了泪水。那个恶魔解开了她的绳索，为她遮挡，质问道：“这不是你的 lovers 吗？”

paragraphs.en: She replied, "I don’t know him; I’ve never seen him before." He growled, "You liar! You will confess!"
paragraphs.zh: 她回答说：“我不认识他；我从没见过这个人。”他怒吼道：“你这个骗子！你会招供的！”

paragraphs.en: She said, "I cannot lie about someone I don’t know."
paragraphs.zh: 她说：“我无法对一个不认识的人撒谎。”

paragraphs.en: He handed her a sword, saying, "Strike his head off if you don't know him." She took the sword and faced me. I signaled with my eyes, and she understood, winking back.
paragraphs.zh: 他递给她一把剑，说：“如果你不认识他，就砍下他的头。”她接过剑，面向我。我使了个眼色，她会意了，冲我眨了眨眼。

paragraphs.en: She then threw the sword away and stepped back, saying, "How can I strike someone I do not know?" The demon retorted, "You cannot kill because he has slept with you. You have suffered this torture without confessing."
paragraphs.zh: 她扔下剑，退后一步，说道：“我不认识这个人，怎么可以打他？”恶魔反驳道：“你不能杀他，因为他曾与你同枕共眠。你承受了这一切折磨却从未承认。”

paragraphs.en: Turning to me, the demon said, "Do you also not recognize her?" I replied, "Who is she? I’ve never seen her before."
paragraphs.zh: 恶魔转向我问道：“你也不认识她吗？”我回答说：“她是谁？我从未见过她。”

paragraphs.en: He challenged, "Then strike her head off and prove you don’t know her." I took the sword and sprang toward her.
paragraphs.zh: 他挑衅道：“那你砍下她的头来证明你根本不认识她。”我拿起剑，朝她扑了过去。

paragraphs.en: The next night, Dinarzad urged her sister Shahrazad: "Tell us the rest of the story." Shahrazad agreed: "Very well."
paragraphs.zh: 第二天晚上，迪纳扎德催促她的妹妹沙赫拉兹黛：“把剩下的故事讲给我们听吧。”沙赫拉兹黛答应了：“好吧。”

paragraphs.en: Shahrazad recounted how the second dervish approached a girl and she winked at him, saying, "Bravo! This is how you repay me!" The dervish understood her meaning and pledged with his eyes that he would give his life for her.
paragraphs.zh: 沙海拉扎德讲述说，第二个苦行僧走近一个女孩，她向他眨了眨眼，说道：“精彩极了！这就是你报答我的方式吗？”苦行僧明白了她的意思，用眼神发誓愿意为她献出生命。

paragraphs.en: They stood silently, exchanging glances as if to say:
paragraphs.zh: 他们默默站立，互相对视了一眼，仿佛在彼此传递着什么意味深长的信息。

paragraphs.en: Many a lover speaks his heart through looks, And with a glance conveys what's in his soul. How sweet are the glances of the eyes, How graceful when passion fills them whole.
paragraphs.zh: 许多恋人通过眼神表达心声，一瞥之间便传达出内心的情感。眼睛的凝视是多么甜蜜，当激情充盈其中时，又是多么优雅。

paragraphs.en: One writes his love with every gaze, Another reads it in his lover’s ways.
paragraphs.zh: 一人以每一眼抒写爱意， 另一人则从恋人举止中读出深情。

paragraphs.en: I threw down my sword, stepped back, and declared, "Even if I must die, I cannot strike a woman I do not know." The demon retorted, "You conspire against me. Witness your fate now."
paragraphs.zh: 我把剑一扔，退后一步，declaring，“即便我因此丧命，也不能对一个陌生女子下手。”恶魔反驳道：“你图谋陷害我。看吧，这是你的下场。”

paragraphs.en: He severed her arms with his sword, sending them flying. As she lay dying, she looked at me and bid farewell with a glance. At that moment, I wished for death and nearly fainted.
paragraphs.zh: 他挥剑砍断了她的双臂，手臂飞了出去。她躺在那里奄奄一息，用最后的目光看了我一眼，与我告别。那一刻，我也渴望死亡，几乎晕了过去。

paragraphs.en: The demon said, "This is the punishment for those who deceive." Turning to me, he added, "If your wife betrays you, you must kill her. I took this girl on her wedding night, when she was just twelve and knew no other man but me.
paragraphs.zh: 恶魔说道：“这是欺骗者的惩罚。”他转向我，补充道：“如果你的妻子背叛了你，你必须杀死她。我是在她的婚礼之夜带走这个女孩的，当时她才十二岁，除了我之外，她不认识其他男人。”

paragraphs.en: I visited her every ten days as a Persian gentleman. When I found out she had deceived me, I killed her. You may be innocent, but I cannot let you go unscathed.
paragraphs.zh: 我每隔十天便以波斯绅士的身份前去探望她。得知她欺骗了我之后，我亲手结束了她的生命。你或许无辜，但我不能让你毫发无伤地离开。

paragraphs.en: Transform into an animal—dog, ass, or lion? Or would you prefer to become a bird?"
paragraphs.zh: 变成动物——狗、驴还是狮子？抑或你更愿意化作一只鸟？

paragraphs.en: I pleaded for mercy, hoping the demon might spare me: "O demon, it is more fitting that you forgive me as the envied forgave his envious foe."
paragraphs.zh: 我恳求他网开一面，希望恶魔能饶过我：“哦，恶魔，请像被嫉妒的人原谅他的嫉妒对手那样宽恕我吧。”

paragraphs.en: The demon asked, "How was that?" and I began my story.
paragraphs.zh: 恶魔问道：“那是怎么回事？”我便开始了我的讲述。
